item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 231745
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 PM EDT Wed Sep 23 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Far Eastern Tropical Atlantic (AL90):
An area of low pressure located a couple of hundred miles southwest
off the coast of western Africa is gradually becoming better
defined, and the associated shower and thunderstorm activity has
increased since yesterday. This system could become a short-lived
tropical depression on Thursday or Friday while it moves
northwestward to northward. However, strong upper-level winds
should end the opportunity for development by the weekend.
Interests in the Cabo Verde Islands should monitor the progress of
this system as gusty winds, areas of heavy rain and flash flooding
is possible there by Friday.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...50 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

Central Subtropical Atlantic (Former Tropical Storm Fay):
Showers and thunderstorms have increased with the remnants of
Fay located several hundred miles southwest of the Azores. While
environmental conditions are only marginally conducive for
development, this system could become a tropical depression again
today or tonight if the current thunderstorm activity persists.
The system is forecast to move westward during the next couple of
days, and by the weekend upper-level winds should inhibit formation
chances.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...70 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

$$
Forecaster Blake

item.description:
Issued at 900 PM GMT Wed Sep 23 2026 
392 
WTNT31 KNHC 232034
TCPAT1
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Fay Advisory Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 PM GMT Wed Sep 23 2026
 
...LOW PRESSURE SYSTEM RE-DEVELOPS INTO TROPICAL DEPRESSION FAY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 PM GMT...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...30.1N 39.2W
ABOUT 885 MI...1425 KM SW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 270 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1011 MB...29.86 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 PM GMT (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Fay was
located near latitude 30.1 North, longitude 39.2 West.  The
depression is moving toward the west near 8 mph (13 km/h) and this 
general motion is expected to continue for the next several days. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Some strengthening is possible during the next couple of days, but 
gradual weakening should occur thereafter. 
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1011 mb (29.86 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 AM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Pasch

item.title: Tropical Depression Fay Forecast Discussion Number 15
item.description:
Issued at 900 PM GMT Wed Sep 23 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 232035
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Depression Fay Discussion Number  15
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 PM GMT Wed Sep 23 2026
 
Convection has redeveloped around the center of Fay and has 
persisted during the day.  An earlier ASCAT pass indicated that the 
system still had a well-defined circulation. Therefore, Fay meets 
the criteria to be classified as a tropical cyclone again.  
The earlier ASCAT pass showed a maximum wind vector of around 
31 kt and the most recent TAFB Dvorak classification was at T1.5/25 
kt.  Based on the given data, Fay's intensity is estimated to be 30 
kt.
 
The cyclone is moving just a little south of due west, or around 
260/8 kt, as it moves to the south of a low- to mid-level ridge to 
the northwest. Fay is expected to continue on this general motion 
for the next several days. The current NHC track forecast is in 
line with the HCCA and GDMI forecast aids.
 
There is a brief opportunity for Fay to regain tropical storm 
status during the next day or so, however wind shear is expected to
increase again after 36 h. This should lead to the cyclone 
gradually weakening again, with the system becoming a post-tropical 
remnant low by 60 h, and then dissipating around 96 h, as 
suggested by simulated satellite imagery from the ECMWF global 
model.  The current NHC intensity forecast track is in line with 
both the HCCA and GDMI forecast aids.
